questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English speaking country to improve my English skills and so there would not be a language barrier between me and the locals. Further I had never been to Australia before and it was a place that I really wanted to visit and I wanted to try to live here.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy the coordinator made some good step-by-step emails of all the things you needed to do and complete. There were a lot of emails though so it was a bit overwhelming but everything was written in the emails. There were also many other exchange students that were trying to enrole to you could also ask them for help or what they had done.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really receive any assistance. I needed to change one of my units so the coordinator helped me doing that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are different campus housing options. I stayed at Queen Mary Building which is the cheapest option where you have your own room but you share the bathroom and kitchen with others. There are also other options as Scape which is a bit more expensive but you live in a flat with 8 people and share a room with one of them.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were no mealplans available where I lived but there were kitchens where you could cook. However they were sometimes a bit busy during “rush hour” around 7pm.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a good way to get to know many other exchange students and people are very chatty in the kitchen. It is nice because it is on campus and also close to the city. However it is quite expensive compared to what you get so I think it might be possible to find something a bit cheaper if you find housing on your own. It can be hard to find housing on your own before you arrive to Sydney but you know if you have housing through the university a few month prior going there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I recieved many emails that explained how to do it and what the next steps in the process were and then I had to choose units I wanted and if they had prerequisites then I should also send a proof that I had these. I found the page where you could find all the different units quite hard to understand and see which units were avaliable and which I could take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were a coordinator, that helped with any questions you might have and she responded to any emails within 5 days.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all of the classes that I wanted but there were one I wanted that had some prerequisites that I didn't met and therefore I was not allowed to have this unit.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a to-do list of the things you need to do and take your time. In some periods there is quite a lot of things you need to do. USYD also offer different units for exchange students as “Learning in outdoor education” and “Sport and learning in Australian culture” and I heard great things about both.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: At USYD you are only allowed to take BA units when you are on your BA. I felt that the academic level was quite similar to UCPH or a bit easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At USYD I had laboratory classes and lectures. In my units there were no theoretical exercises as I have in UCPH. Further there are many small quizzes, tests, assignments and presentations during the semester that all count as a small part of the overall grade for a unit, so the final exam only count 50-60% of the final grade. They record all lectures but watch them during the semester so you are not super busy in the study vacation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: “Microbes, Infection and immunity”, “Neuroscience in health and disease”, “Biochemistry of human disease” and “Beyond the genome”

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend “Beyond the genome” to exchange students because Stuart the lecturer is really good and passionate about the unit and content. Further it is very relevant and new methods that he teaches about which makes this unit very relevant for students within the biochemistry, microbiology and biomedicine field of study.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't have many unexpected costs but I was a bit surprised that the prizes in the supermarket was more expensive than in Denmark. I also used more on weekendtrips and holidays during the semester than I expected to do before the exchange.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The vegetables and diary products are more expensive, but bying meat and take away is generally cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are all kind of sports clubs that you can join if you have any sport that you do in Denmark or a new sport you want to try. They also have many different cultural societies, hiking societies, chocolate society and choir. They have all different societies you can imagine. I was a part of yoga society, bushwalkers, dance society and the choir, and all of them were great fun.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think the bushwalker society is a good one to join because they arrange many trips so you can go out in the nature on different hikes to places that you might no go yourself and together with people that also wants to explore more of the country and area around Sydney.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really recommend going for a weekend trip to Blue Mountains. You can also do canoeing in the Blue Mountains. The area south of Sydney with Royal national park and Jervis bay is also really nice. There is also many nice costal walks around Sydney. North of Sydney by New Castle is also nice and Hunter Valley is also worth a visit. It is also possible to take the plane for a weekendtrip to Brisbane and the area around or to Melbourne. There is also one week off during the semester where you can eg. can go to Tasmania or do an East Coast road trip. Also if you have the time after the semester then visit New Zealand, that is amazing!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to adjust to the local culture because it is not so different from Danish culture and everyone speaks English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be a bit hard to socialize with Australian students, but the best way to do it is in the classes and if there is groupwork then try to form a group with the local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I had to adjust a bit to speaking English all the time and express myself in English but within the first few weeks it felt normal

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated that everyone was so helpful and kind and also very chatty.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress to much about socializing right in the beginning, it will come slowly and you will get friends!
Take your time to explore both Sydney and the area around. The nature is so pretty and it has so much to offer.
Enjoy every moment of it because time goes super fast so before you know the semester is over and you will return back home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attend all the activities in the beginning of the semester it is a good way to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was all the travels and small trips I was able to do in Sydney and around Sydney while I was studying. I really enjoy travelling so it was very nice to be able to combine it with studying.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge for me was the FOMO I got when I saw other people were doing fun things that I was not a part of. Sometimes it was just because I needed to relax so I chose to stay home, but I had to remind myself that they would still be my friends eventhough I was not a part of every single activity and that I couldn't see all of Australia in 5 months.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
